seoTitle: How to Format Question Text in Microsoft Forms
metaDescription: Microsoft Forms has no font-family picker, but it does let you bold, resize, and recolor question text. Here's where that toolbar hides and what Style controls instead.
intro: Microsoft Forms doesn't give you a font-family picker: the interface typeface stays the same across every form, by design, so it renders consistently on any device a respondent opens. What it does offer is more than most guides on this topic mention. Highlighting text inside a question title, subtitle, or description brings up a floating toolbar with bold, italic, underline, font size, font color, and list formatting, according to Microsoft's own support documentation. Separately, the Style button changes the form's overall theme and background. This guide covers both: the text-formatting toolbar that's easy to miss, and the theme controls that get discussed more often.

steps.heading: Open your form in the builder
steps.body: From forms.office.com, open My forms to see everything built so far, organized under Recent, My forms, Filled forms, and Shared with me, with a Favorites tab alongside. Each card shows the form's title, owner, and response count, useful for finding an existing form to restyle instead of starting from scratch.

image.caption: The Forms landing page, listing existing forms with response counts under Recent, My forms, and Filled forms.

steps.heading: Format question text with the built-in toolbar
steps.body: Click into any question title, subtitle, or description and highlight a word or phrase. A floating toolbar appears with Bold, Italic, Underline, Font color, Font size, Numbering, and Bullets, per Microsoft's own support documentation. This is the part most articles on this topic skip: Forms does have text formatting, it's just scoped to styling the existing typeface instead of swapping it for another one. Keyboard shortcuts work too: Ctrl or Cmd plus B for bold, I for italic, U for underline.

steps.heading: Use Style for theme and background, not font
steps.body: Inside any form, the top toolbar holds Style, Settings, Preview, and Collect responses, in that order, on every screen of the builder. Style opens a set of preset themes and background images applied to the whole form's cover and background. It changes color and imagery, not the typeface. Font family stays fixed across every Forms survey regardless of which theme is active.

steps.heading: Set your form's cover details
steps.body: The cover section at the top of the form holds the title, an optional date, and a description, layered over the theme's background image or color. Since the typeface itself can't change, the size, bold, and color controls from the text-formatting toolbar are what shift emphasis here. A bolded or enlarged title reads differently from the plain default even though the underlying font stays the same.

image.caption: A form's cover section, showing the title, date, and description overlaid on the selected theme's background image.

steps.heading: Combine formatting with structure for real hierarchy
steps.body: With actual formatting tools in the picture, hierarchy in a form comes from combining them with structure: a bolded or resized question title, short and direct wording, and the right field type for the answer. Rating and multiple-choice fields do more scannable work than a paragraph of styled text. Each question also carries a Required toggle and extra options under its "..." menu, which control behavior, not appearance. Formatting is easy to overuse; a form where every title is bold reads as noisy, not organized.

image.caption: A set of multiple-choice questions in the builder, showing how formatting and question structure work together.

steps.heading: Preview and collect responses
steps.body: Click Preview at the top of the canvas to see the form exactly as a respondent will, including how the theme, cover details, and any text formatting look together. Once satisfied, use Collect responses to generate the shareable link. This is also a good moment to check that the theme and formatting read well against your organization's branding if the form is going out externally.

faq.question: Can I change the font family in Microsoft Forms?
faq.answer: No. Forms locks its interface typeface across every form for consistent rendering on any device. There is no font-family picker for question text.

faq.question: Can I make question text bold, bigger, or a different color?
faq.answer: Yes. Highlight text in a question title, subtitle, or description and a floating toolbar appears with Bold, Italic, Underline, Font color, and Font size, according to Microsoft's own support documentation. This works even though the underlying typeface can't be swapped.

faq.question: What does the Style button change, if not the font?
faq.answer: It opens a set of preset themes and background images that change the form's overall color scheme and cover background, not the typeface or size of the text.

faq.question: How do I make an important question stand out?
faq.answer: Combine the text-formatting toolbar (bold, size, color) with structure: a short, direct title and the right field type for the answer. Bolding every question cancels out the emphasis, so use it selectively.

faq.question: Where can I see how my form will look to respondents?
faq.answer: Click Preview in the top toolbar of the builder. It shows the form as sent, including the selected theme, cover layout, and any text formatting applied to questions.

verifiedNote: Screens and click path (My forms list, cover section, question builder) come from a recorded walkthrough. The claim that Forms has no text formatting at all was checked against Microsoft's own support documentation in September 2026 and found wrong: Forms provides bold, italic, underline, font size, font color, numbering, and bullets for question text through a floating toolbar; it just has no font-family picker. The previous draft stated flatly that text styling wasn't available and framed structure as the only lever, which this rewrite corrects throughout.
